claim: The launch-12 capacity bump 16,384 -> 32,768 (+38,010,880 B g_bridge_vmmap + 3x 786,432 B 24-B-record arrays) adds +20,553,728 B (+19.60 MiB) BSS to a shipped PRX whose measured .bss is 21,558,752 B (20.56 MiB); the resulting 42,112,480 B (40.16 MiB) BSS in a 40,188,672 B (16 KiB-aligned) writable segment of a 74,978,914 B (71.51 MiB) total PT_LOAD memsz image is AFFORDABLE: 815x under the only documented machine cap (MAXDSIZ 32 GiB, pinned sdk-v0.43 machine/vmparam.h) and only 1.378x the total-image memsz and 2.05x the BSS already proven by >=6 real console boots of the same runtime class.
verdict_honest_unknown: No PS5 dynlib/PRX-loader-specific per-module BSS or segment-memsz cap is documented anywhere in the pinned SDK (sdk-v0.43); kernel-internal behavior (loader segment allocation policy, sysctl KERN_PROC_VMMAP temp-buffer sizing for a 36.25 MiB request) is unverifiable from the pin. Empirical bounds are therefore the operative constraint: 51.90 MiB total PT_LOAD memsz / 20.56 MiB BSS loaded, started (module_start_return=0) and fully walked (22,761-record vmmap sysctl into the 19,005,440 B buffer) on every observed boot.

shipped_prx.elf: ELF64 LSB, e_machine 62 (x86-64), e_type 65048 (0xFE08, prospero PRX), 5 PT_LOADs, 27 sections

composed_object_bss.note: All other linked objects contribute 92 B NOBITS; PRX .bss exceeds object sum by 4,793 B of link alignment. runtime_start_bridge.o (19,796,470 B NOBITS) is the same translation unit's standalone compile, not linked into l10-2.
composed_object_bss.lmf_hunk_status: kMaxVmMappings is still 1024 in the shipped l10-2 artifact (24 KiB array); the EDITION.json edit-4 staged header override (1024->16384) did NOT reach this composition, exactly the risk CAPTURE-CAPACITY.md section 5.1 flags for verification in launch-12.

window_anchor_mappings.note: 4th scaling array; omitted from CAPTURE-CAPACITY.md section 5.3 list but scales with kBridgeVmmapEntries and must be budgeted

lmf_capture_mappings.note: 1024 -> 32768 = the section-5.1 fold (16384) plus the section-5.2 bump (32768) combined

spanpub_top16_table.note: kMaxPublishedSpans=16 x 24 B; bounded window, orthogonal to snapshot capacity (fixture C3)

documented_pinned_sdk.reading: FreeBSD-derived per-process data-size cap 32 GiB; the post-bump writable segment (40.2 MiB) sits 815x under it. Headers carry no prospero dynlib/PRX-specific per-module cap.

not_documented: Any PS5 dynlib loader (sceKernelLoadStartModule) per-module BSS, per-segment memsz, or total-module-memory cap: absent from pinned SDK headers (libkernel.h has only uint32_t SceKernelModuleSegmentInfo.size reporting fields), ldscript (no MEMORY/LENGTH caps), and docs.
Kernel-side temp-buffer policy for sysctl KERN_PROC_VMMAP with a 38,010,880 B len request (works at 19,005,440 B request with ~19 MiB of real map data, 6/6 boots).

frozen_prx_baseline.proves: total-image loading (~30.7 MiB memsz) is not the binding constraint; its BSS is only 70.3 KiB so it proves NOTHING about BSS headroom

current_class_console_boots.evidence: worker-verdict-first-real runs 1/2/3 (pids 317/341/355) + launch10-prep run5 baselines (session 370, three boots)
current_class_console_boots.bridge_walk: bridge_vmentry_entries=22761/22761/10028/10028/9993/9993, bridge_vm_walk_stop=0 on all six; the 19,005,440 B g_bridge_vmmap buffer fully exercised by sysctl + per-record walk every boot
current_class_console_boots.spanpub: bridge_spanpub_cap=1 saturated on every observed >16384 boot
current_class_console_boots.refusals_seen: PS5Pad.ini ASCII / loadlist size / pad phase=6 (config-class, code=3/-8) - never a memory-class failure
current_class_console_boots.proves: 54,425,186 B total PT_LOAD memsz with 21,558,752 B BSS (>=19.5 MiB of it physically resident during the walk) loads and starts on the target

verdict_rationale.documented_limit_margin: 40,188,672 B writable segment vs MAXDSIZ 34,359,738,368 B = 815x margin
verdict_rationale.empirical_margin: 1.378x the total-image memsz and 2.05x the BSS of a runtime class that booted >=6 times with zero memory-class failures; the dominant BSS consumer (g_bridge_vmmap) is already proven resident at 18.12 MiB
verdict_rationale.residency_cost: worst-case all-BSS-resident adds ~40.2 MiB (~0.3% of a ~12.5 GiB title-class budget); the walk already touches the full raw buffer on every boot
verdict_rationale.binding_constraint: none identified at the operating point; the honest unknown is an undocumented kernel-internal cap, for which the 6-boot record gives no positive signal of existence

alternative_lever_bounded_proposal.status: not required by this verdict; proposal-only
alternative_lever_bounded_proposal.sketch: Keep kBridgeVmmapEntries=16384. The walk already parses EVERY record (bridge_vmentry_entries=22761) - only the SNAPSHOT copy is bounded. Feed bridge_spanpub_publish from the walk stream instead of the 16,384-record prefix so interest-spans above the prefix cut (tail/heap-top) register into the existing bounded top-16 table, and define the published envelope over the FULL walk. Zero added BSS; changes are confined to the publish input + envelope semantics.
alternative_lever_bounded_proposal.contract_warning: This changes the caller-contract pin (D1: envelope = max end over the CAPTURED prefix; 'omitted <=> at/above envelope', fixture T5's 'honest unmapped below the cut'). A full-walk envelope removes the truncation class entirely for span queries, so the validator's capture-truncated refusal and fixture H5/E4/T* expectations must be re-derived; it is a NEW bounded revision, not a loosening of the validator.
alternative_lever_bounded_proposal.requires: new distinct IDs, host fixture re-derivation first, no resubmission of any refused launch
